Read and validate a calibration setup table

Source: R/calibrar-main.R
calibration_setup.Rd

Read a calibration settings table from a text file and coerce it to the structure expected by calibration_data() and calibration_objFn(). The setup table defines which model outputs are compared with observations, which objective function is used for each output, whether a row contributes to the calibration, and how each component is weighted in the final objective.

Usage

calibration_setup(file, control = list(), ...)

Arguments

file

Path to the calibration setup file, typically a .csv file.

control

Named list of defaults used when optional columns are missing from the setup table. Currently recognised entries are:

col_skip

Default number of leading columns to discard when a text file is read as a full table by calibration_data(). Defaults to 2.

nrows

Default number of rows to read from each data file. Defaults to NA, which is interpreted downstream as “read all rows”.

...

Additional arguments passed to utils::read.csv() when reading file.

Value

A data.frame describing the calibration targets. The returned table is suitable for direct use in calibration_data() and calibration_objFn(). Standard columns are coerced to the expected types and missing optional columns are added where needed.

Details

The function is a validated wrapper around utils::read.csv(). It checks required column names, coerces standard column types, fills a few optional columns from control, and derives weight from cv when needed.

The setup table may contain the following columns:

variable

Name of the calibration component. This name must match the corresponding element returned by the model function supplied to calibration_objFn().

type

Name of the objective function used for that component. In current workflows this is usually the name of a function accepted by objFn(), such as "norm2", "lnorm2", "pois", "multinom", "normp", or "penalty".

calibrate

Logical flag indicating whether the component is active in the calibration. Only rows with calibrate = TRUE are included in the objective function returned by calibration_objFn().

weight

Positive weight used when partial objective values are aggregated. If weight is missing, or contains NA, it is derived from cv as 1 / (2 * cv^2) for the corresponding rows.

cv

Coefficient of variation used to derive weight when an explicit weight is not supplied. At least one of weight or cv must be available in the table.

use_data

Logical flag indicating whether an observed dataset must be read for that row. This is typically FALSE for pure penalties such as "normp", where the objective depends only on simulated values.

file

Path to the observed data file for that component. Paths are interpreted relative to the path argument of calibration_data(). This column is still required when use_data = FALSE, although the file will not be read in that case.

varid

Optional identifier used by calibration_data() when extracting a single column from a text file. If omitted, a full numeric table is read instead.

col_skip

Optional number of leading columns to discard when a text file is read as a full table. Missing values are replaced by control$col_skip.

nrows

Optional number of rows to read from each observed-data file. Missing values are replaced by control$nrows.

Required columns are variable, type, calibrate, use_data, and file. In addition, at least one of weight or cv must be supplied.

Weight handling

Aggregation weights are stored in the returned table regardless of whether the objective is later used in vector or scalar form.

If the table does not contain a weight column, weights are computed from cv as 1 / (2 * cv^2). If weight exists but contains missing values, those entries are filled using the same formula. All final weights must be strictly positive.

Relationship with the rest of the workflow

A typical file-based calibration workflow is:

  1. read the setup table with calibration_setup();

  2. load observed data with calibration_data();

  3. build the objective function with calibration_objFn();

  4. pass the resulting function to calibrate() or another optimiser.

See also

calibration_data(), calibration_objFn(), calibrate(), objFn()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
demo = calibrar_demo(model = "PredatorPrey")
setup = calibration_setup(file = demo$setup)
setup
} # }
